quizzes.title: Dirac Medal Recognition
quizzes.passage: The Dirac Medal is an award that honours the legacy of Paul Dirac, a physicist whose name is attached to it. The award is given for pioneering work. In 2026 the medal went to Deepak Dhar together with other physicists, and their work was in one scientific area. The medal is presented by an international body that works in theoretical physics. The booklet covers the award in its AWARDS section, alongside brief notes on the award's background and the prize each recipient receives.

questions.q: The 2026 Dirac Medal recognised pioneering work in which field?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the 2026 award honoured pioneering work in statistical mechanics.

questions.q: How often is the Dirac Medal presented?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the Dirac Medal as an annual award.

questions.q: Paul Dirac is described in the booklet as one of the founders of which field?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes Dirac as one of the founders of modern quantum mechanics.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The 2026 Dirac Medal was a shared award.
Reason (R): Bernard Derrida also won the 2026 medal alongside Deepak Dhar.
options: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R explains A
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, and Derrida's joint win is the reason the 2026 medal was shared.

questions.q: Which of the following was a 2026 co-winner of the Dirac Medal?
questions.explanation: Haim Sompolinsky is named in the booklet as one of the 2026 co-winners.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 2026 award:
I. The 2026 Dirac Medal recognised pioneering work in statistical mechanics.
II. The Dirac Medal is presented once a year.
III. Deepak Dhar was the only physicist to win the 2026 Dirac Medal.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while III is wrong because Dhar shared the medal with others.

questions.q:
Based on the booklet, how many of the statements below are accurate?
I. The 2026 Dirac Medal recognised work in statistical mechanics.
II. Paul Dirac is described as one of the founders of modern quantum mechanics.
III. The Dirac Medal is presented every decade.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are in the booklet and III is not, so exactly two are accurate.

quizzes.title: Dirac Medal Facts Check
quizzes.passage: The AILET Corner section of the booklet includes an AWARDS entry on a medal presented in 2026. The medal went to Dhar and other physicists for pioneering work in one scientific area. The award is named after a physicist who helped found a branch of physics, and it honours that physicist's legacy. The medal is presented by an international centre for theoretical physics. Each recipient receives a prize along with the medal.

questions.q: In which branch of physics was the 2026 award-winning work done? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the 2026 Dirac Medal honoured pioneering work in statistical mechanics.

questions.q: Paul Dirac is one of the founders of which branch of physics? (two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet calls Dirac one of the founders of modern quantum mechanics.

questions.q: How often is the Dirac Medal presented? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the Dirac Medal as an annual award.

questions.q: What is the surname of the 2026 co-winner whose first name is Haim?
questions.explanation: Haim Sompolinsky is named as one of the 2026 co-winners.

questions.q: What is the first name of the 2026 co-winner whose surname is Derrida?
questions.explanation: Bernard Derrida is named as one of the 2026 co-winners.

questions.q: In which month's Current Affairs issue does the AWARDS section appear? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet is titled Current Affairs August 2026.

questions.q: What is the surname of the physicist whose legacy the medal honours? (surname only)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the medal honours the legacy of Paul Dirac.
